title: Buried where he died
hook: he dies in Aisha's room and is buried there, now beneath the green dome in Medina

segments.voice: Yesterday, the last days: he gave away his last coins, left nothing behind, and asked that the prayer be kept. Your line was keep the prayer. What did you give away? Day seven hundred ninety-seven.

A curtain hangs where a door would be. Outside it, the companions have lined up for the dawn prayer, and Abu Bakr is leading it. Then, Anas reports in Bukhari, the curtain lifts. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, looks out at the rows of people praying, and he smiles. The people nearly break their lines for joy. He signals to them to finish, and lets the curtain fall. That glance through the curtain is one of the last things they see of him. The room behind that curtain, beside the mosque, is Aisha's. Today, what happens in it, and why it is still there.
screen: `A ROOM BESIDE THE MOSQUE.` → `THE CURTAIN LIFTS.` → `HE SMILES AT THE ROWS.`

segments.voice: Aisha tells the next part herself. In her account in Bukhari, he died in her house, on the day that was hers, with his head resting against her. Her brother had come in with a fresh tooth-stick, and she saw the Prophet's eyes follow it, so she softened it for him and he used it. Small, ordinary care, right at the end. Then the question of where to bury him. The companions did not agree. Abu Bakr settled it, according to a report in Tirmidhi, by remembering something he had heard the Prophet say: a prophet is buried in the place where he dies. So they did not carry him out to a graveyard. They dug in the floor of the room, where the bed had been. Buried where he died. That room is still there. Over time the mosque grew around it, and today it sits inside the Prophet's Mosque, under a green dome. Visitors stand before it and greet him: peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. And that greeting points to a verse. Surah al-Ahzab, verse fifty-six, in Pickthall's words: "Lo! Allah and His angels shower blessings on the Prophet. O ye who believe! Ask blessings on him and salute him with a worthy salutation." This is salawat. Muslims say a short blessing after his name: salla Allahu alayhi wa sallam, God bless him and grant him peace. It is the little mark you see written after his name. So the burial and the blessing belong together. The body rests in one room. The greeting goes everywhere. This is where the long story of his life, the whole sirah we have walked since this block began, comes to rest: Sumayyah, the boycott, Ta'if, the cave, Quba, the treaty, Mecca's open doors, the farewell at Arafah. And tomorrow the story turns to the people he left.
screen: `SHE SOFTENED THE TOOTH-STICK.` · `A PROPHET IS BURIED WHERE HE DIES.` · `A ROOM UNDER A GREEN DOME.` · `ASK BLESSINGS ON HIM.` · then, large: `PEACE UPON HIM.`

segments.voice: The practice: send peace. Sit, and let your breathing slow. Bring to mind the small room: the curtain, the bed, the tooth-stick, the rows of people praying outside. If you pray, you can say the salawat Muslims use, salla Allahu alayhi wa sallam, quietly, a few times, at the pace of your breath. If you don't pray, stay with the word peace, and let it go out to everyone who has ever carried this story to you. Either way, end on one slow breath. The bell holds the time.
Salawat, the blessing Muslims add after the Prophet's name, said at the room beside the mosque where, by a saying Abu Bakr remembered, he was buried where he died. Today's word.
Your line: peace upon him. Today, when you hear his name, or any name you love, add a word of peace after it, out loud or under your breath. Day seven hundred ninety-seven.

howItsDone: Muslims add a blessing of peace (salla Allahu alayhi wa sallam) whenever the Prophet is named, and visitors to the Prophet's Mosque in Medina stand before his resting place and greet him with peace.

fork.setup: you're among the companions. the Prophet has died in Aisha's room, and people disagree about where to bury him. what do you do?
options: carry him to the graveyard with the others.
carry him back to Mecca, where he was born.
bury him in the room where he died.
fork.reveal: Abu Bakr remembered him saying that a prophet is buried where he dies, so they dug in the floor of the room.

original.note: Arabic: God bless him and grant him peace, said after the Prophet's name.

trapdoor: what you thought: a detail about a burial.
what it means: he was laid to rest in the room where he died, and the greeting of peace goes on everywhere.
what a scholar hears: the report in Tirmidhi that Abu Bakr recalled, and the room of Aisha, now inside the Prophet's Mosque.
